alt: Poster: SEBI circular of 5 Nov 2026 - single USD 5 million notional limit for INR currency derivatives without underlying exposure, combined across all INR pairs and exchanges; conditions above the limit for FPIs and domestic clients
text:
A single USD 5 million limit now governs rupee currency derivatives positions taken without underlying exposure.

SEBI's circular of 5 November 2026 (HO/(561)2026-MRD-POD2/I/25177/2026) revises the underlying-exposure requirement for currency derivatives. Domestic clients and FPIs may take long or short positions up to USD 5 million equivalent of notional value, outstanding at any point, without establishing underlying exposure. The limit is a single figure counted across all currency pairs involving INR, put together, and combined across all recognised stock exchanges.

Beyond that limit, the conditions differ. FPIs must keep short positions across exchanges and FCY-INR pairs within USD 5 million, and long positions above it need underlying exposure in Indian debt or equity securities, including units of equity or debt mutual funds. Domestic clients may exceed USD 5 million subject to the RBI conditions specified in the circular. Exchanges and clearing corporations are to put the necessary systems in place and inform members.

Our view: the combined, cross-exchange measurement makes position tracking across venues part of compliance. That is an interpretation, not advice.

For practitioners: how are you or your clients planning to monitor aggregate INR currency derivatives notional across exchanges?
